messages.body_plain:
Hi:

Here are a few ways you could go about it using plyr functions.

null.output <- data.frame(richness = factor(rep(2:8, 4)),
                          metric = rnorm(28, 10, 1),
                          metric2 = rnorm(28, 1, 1),
                          metric3 = rnorm(7.5, 1, 1))

##### Method 1: Use numcolwise().

# Function to compute summaries from a variable v
f <- function(v) c(iterations = length(v),
                   average = mean(v, na.rm = TRUE),
                   lower = quantile(v, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                   upper = quantile(v, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))

# Apply f to each numeric variable in null.output, by richness
u <- ddply(null.output, .(richness), numcolwise(f))

# Names didn't get attached, so put these into each set of four rows
summnames <- c("iterations", "average", "lower", "upper")
u$summary <- summnames
head(u)

##### Method 2: Write a function that returns all of the summaries
#####                 for each input variable as a vector.

summfun <- function(d)
{
     # Create the output variable names
     vars <- names(d)[grepl("metric", names(d))]
     snames <- c("iterations", "average", "lower", "upper")
     vnames <- paste(rep(vars, each = length(summnames)),
                     rep(snames, length(vars)), sep = ".")

     # Function to be applied to each variable
     g <- function(x) c(length(x), mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE))

     # Convert the numeric part of the data frame to matrix
     # and then apply the function g to each column
     L <- apply(data.matrix(d[, vars]), 2, g)

     # String the matrix in column order to a vector, attach
     # the names to it, then return
     v <- as.vector(L)
     names(v) <- vnames
     v
}

w <- ddply(null.output, .(richness), summfun)

# Another way to display the output:

library(reshape2)
dm <- melt(w, id = "richness")
dcast(dm, variable ~ richness, value.var = "value")

Hopefully one of these appeals to you...

Dennis

messages.subject: Passing a variable "size" argument to sample() with ddply
messages.subject_clean: Passing a variable "size" argument to sample() with ddply
messages.body_plain:
I want to extract random samples from a data set ("data") of oceanographic measurements collected throughout the water column (0-200 m) and over 20 degrees of latitude. I have defined 5 strata in depth and 5 strata in latitude, for a total of 25 strata from which to draw the samples. Since I'm interested in obtaining a specific (but variable) number of samples from each stratum, I have generated a vector listing how many samples to draw from each one (the "size" argument in sample()).

The code I've written to do this is as follows:

# Define the latitude strata:
brks.lat <- c(30.342, 33.418, 34.182, 35.02, 36.87, 47)
# Define the depth strata:
brks.dep <- c(0, 10, 30, 60, 100, 200)

# Create 5 grouping factors for latitude and 5 for depth, defined by the breaks vectors:
data$grp.lat <- cut(data$lat, brks.lat, include.lowest = TRUE)
data$grp.dep <- cut(data$obsDep, brks.dep, include.lowest = TRUE)

# Obtain the number of observations in each latitude/depth combination (25 total):
nObs <- count(data, c("grp.lat", "grp.dep")) # creates a "freq" column with the observation count in each stratum

# Obtain the minimum number of observations in each depth group across all latitude groups.
nObs.min.dep <- ddply(nObs, .(grp.dep), mutate,
                    nObs.min = min(freq))
# "nObs.min.dep" is the "size" argument to pass to sample()

# Create a column with row index in order to preserve it, since plyr does not keep it and we want to use it for indexing (sampling):
data <- name_rows(data) # creates a data$.rownames column

# Obtain a random sample from each lat/depth combination based on the smallest number of observations in each depth group:
row.samp <- ddply(data, .(grp.lat, grp.dep), summarize,
                  idx = sample(.rownames, size = nObs.min.dep$nObs.min))

Here is where I run into problems. The error I get is:
"Error in sample(.rownames, size = nObs.min.dep$nObs.min) :
   cannot take a sample larger than the population when 'replace = FALSE'"

If I can get it to work, I would use "row.samp$idx" to extract the random observations:

# Extract these samples from the data set:
data2 <- data[as.numeric(row.samp$idx), ]

Any help will be appreciated. I searched earlier posts and found two that were somewhat similar:
ddply/sample() question
https://groups.google.com/forum/?hl=en&fromgroups=#!searchin/manipulatr/sample(/manipulatr/idOdlaonHFc/kACydANHwUEJ
Sampling with plyr
https://groups.google.com/forum/?hl=en&fromgroups=#!searchin/manipulatr/sample(/manipulatr/e44taMKUBJ8/IfrkiVnZmWcJ
However, they did not address the question of how to pass a variable sample size to sample(), which is the part where I'm getting stuck.

Thanks,

Daniel

lm_extract <- function(L)  data.frame(model.frame.lm(L),

ddply(my_data, "group", lm_extract)

from A, and since the output from lm_extract() is not directly from
the original data frame, it fails in the same way yours did. What
ddply() is doing in this case is the equivalent of lapply ->
do.call(rbind, output of lapply).

You can see the problem if you try to assign the row names of the
input data frame inside the function - let's use Ista's version for
illustration:

lm_extract <- function(DF) {
  DF$u <- rownames(DF)
  mod <- lm(y ~ x, data = DF)
  DF$fitted <- fitted(mod)
  DF$residuals <- residuals(mod)
  DF
}

Hi Dennis,

Sure, I'm not arguing against an option to keep the original row names
(nor am I arguing for it). I am arguing that for this particular
application you don't need them. Here is how I understood the original
question:

## make up a data frame including variables not used in the model

my_data <- data.frame(
  x = 1:10,
  y = 1:10 + rnorm(10),
  group = rep(c("A","B"), 5, 2),

  a = rep(1, 10),
  b = rep(2, 10)
)

## Run the model on subsets
my_models <- dlply(my_data, .(group), function(df) {

  lm(y ~ x, data = df)

})

## Extract the predicted and residual values
library(plyr)
(my_data_stats <- ldply(my_models, function(df) {
  data.frame(
    model.frame.lm(df),
    fitted = predict(df),
    resid  = residuals(df)
  )}
))

# Question: The crutial row/case names are gone, so there's

# no path left back to the original data!

# How can I combine my_data_stats with my_data?

## Answer: don't drop variables from the original data set
(my_data2 <- ddply(my_data, "group", function(DF) {

  m <- lm(y ~ x, data=DF)
  DF$resid <- resid(m)
  DF$fitted <- predict(m)
  return(DF)

}))

## my_data2 contains all of my_data plus my_data_stats.
## No need for rownames or merging!

Best,
Ista
